process.label: Flush into objects' infill
process.tooltip: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' infills. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. If the walls are printed with transparent filament, the mixed color infill will be visible. It will not take effect unless the prime tower is enabled.

process.label: Flush into this object
process.tooltip: This object will be used to purge the nozzle after a filament change to save filament and decrease the print time. Colors of the objects will be mixed as a result. It will not take effect unless the prime tower is enabled.

process.label: Flush into objects' support
process.tooltip: Purging after filament change will be done inside objects' support. This may lower the amount of waste and decrease the print time. It will not take effect unless a prime tower is enabled.

process.label: Use beam interlocking
process.tooltip: Generate interlocking beam structure at the locations where different filaments touch. This improves the adhesion between filaments, especially models printed in different materials.

process.label: Toolchange ordering
process.tooltip:
Determines the order of tool changes on each layer.
- Default: Starts with the last used extruder to minimize tool changes.
- Cyclic: Uses a fixed tool sequence each layer. This sacrifices speed for better surface quality, as the extra toolchanges allow layers more time to cool.

process.label: Cyclic order
process.tooltip:
Custom filament sequence used by the cyclic toolchange ordering, as filament numbers separated by commas (e.g. "3,2,1,4").
Each layer prints its filaments following this sequence; filaments not listed are printed last, in ascending order.
Leave empty to cycle through the filaments in ascending order.

process.label: Apply cyclic order to first layer
process.tooltip:
Applies the cyclic toolchange order to the first layer as well.
By default this is disabled, because the first layer is instead ordered for the best bed adhesion: filaments that print small, fragile first-layer features are printed last, so the following tool changes and travel moves are less likely to knock those weakly anchored parts loose. This first-layer order also honors a custom first layer filament sequence when one is set. The cyclic order's benefit (extra tool changes give each layer more time to cool) does not apply to the first layer, which is printed slowly and hot for adhesion.
Enable this only if you need the exact same tool sequence on every layer, including the first, at the cost of that adhesion optimization.

process.label: Interface shells
process.tooltip: Force the generation of solid shells between adjacent materials/volumes. Useful for multi-extruder prints with translucent materials or manual soluble support material.

process.label: Maximum width of a segmented region
process.tooltip: Maximum width of a segmented region. A value of 0 disables this feature.

process.label: Interlocking depth of a segmented region
process.tooltip: Interlocking depth of a segmented region. On every other layer, the segmented region is limited to this depth. It will be ignored if "interlocking_beam" is enabled. Zero disables this feature.

process.label: Interlocking beam width
process.tooltip: The width of the interlocking structure beams.

process.label: Interlocking direction
process.tooltip: Orientation of interlock beams.

process.label: Interlocking beam layers
process.tooltip: The height of the beams of the interlocking structure, measured in number of layers. Less layers is stronger, but more prone to defects.

process.label: Interlocking depth
process.tooltip: The distance from the boundary between filaments to generate interlocking structure, measured in cells. Too few cells will result in poor adhesion.

process.label: Interlocking boundary avoidance
process.tooltip: The distance from the outside of a model where interlocking structures will not be generated, measured in cells.

process.label: Skirt loops
process.tooltip: This is the number of loops for the skirt. 0 means the skirt is disabled.

process.label: Skirt type
process.tooltip: Combined - single skirt for all objects, Per object - individual object skirt.

process.label: Skirt minimum extrusion length
process.tooltip:
Minimum filament extrusion length in mm when printing the skirt. Zero means this feature is disabled.

Using a non-zero value is useful if the printer is set up to print without a prime line.
Final number of loops is not taking into account while arranging or validating objects distance. Increase loop number in such case.

process.label: Skirt distance
process.tooltip: This is the distance from the skirt to the brim or the object.

process.label: Skirt start point
process.tooltip: Angle from the object center to skirt start point. Zero is the most right position, counter clockwise is positive angle.

process.label: Skirt speed
process.tooltip: Speed of skirt, in mm/s. Zero means use default layer extrusion speed.

process.label: Skirt height
process.tooltip: Number of skirt layers: usually only one

process.label: Draft shield
process.tooltip:
A draft shield is useful to protect an ABS or ASA print from warping and detaching from print bed due to wind draft. It is usually needed only with open frame printers, i.e. without an enclosure.

Enabled = skirt is as tall as the highest printed object. Otherwise 'Skirt height' is used.

process.label: Single loop after first layer
process.tooltip: Limits the skirt/draft shield loops to one wall after the first layer. This is useful, on occasion, to conserve filament but may cause the draft shield/skirt to warp / crack.

process.label: Brim type
process.tooltip: This controls the generation of the brim at outer and/or inner side of models. Auto means the brim width is analyzed and calculated automatically.

process.label: Brim width
process.tooltip: This is the distance from the model to the outermost brim line.

process.label: Leading brim length
process.tooltip:
Belt printers only. Extends the brim AHEAD of the object along the belt, on every downhill-facing edge of its contact area - both the object's first contact with the belt and any island that lands later. This apron is laid onto the belt before the object reaches it, so the leading edge has something already stuck down to hold on to.

Measured on the belt surface, and added on top of Brim width: the brim reaches Brim-object gap + Leading brim length + Brim width ahead of the object. Set Brim-object gap to 0, or the apron will not touch the object it is meant to anchor.

On a tilted belt each layer lays one strip of the brim, so the thickness of the resulting brim sheet is set by flow rather than by layer height. Use Brim flow ratio to tune it.

Set to 0 to disable.

process.label: Extra brim width
process.tooltip:
Belt printers only. Widens the brim SIDEWAYS, across the belt, without extending it further ahead of or behind the object. Use it when a part needs more grip along its length than Brim width alone gives.

Measured on the belt surface, and added on top of Brim width: the brim reaches Brim-object gap + Brim width + Extra brim width to either side of the object. To extend the brim ahead of the object instead, use Leading brim length.

Set to 0 to disable.

process.label: Brim-object gap
process.tooltip: This creates a gap between the innermost brim line and the object and can make the brim easier to remove.

process.label: Brim flow ratio
process.tooltip:
This factor affects the amount of material for brims.

The actual brim flow used is calculated by multiplying this value by the filament flow ratio, and if set, the object's flow ratio.

Note: The resulting value will not be affected by the first-layer flow ratio.

process.label: Brim follows compensated outline
process.tooltip:
When enabled, the brim is aligned with the first-layer perimeter geometry after Elephant Foot Compensation is applied.
This option is intended for cases where Elephant Foot Compensation significantly alters the first-layer footprint.

If your current setup already works well, enabling it may be unnecessary and can cause the brim to fuse with upper layers.

process.label: Combine brims
process.tooltip: Combine multiple brims into one when they are close to each other. This can improve brim adhesion.

process.label: Brim ear max angle
process.tooltip:
Maximum angle to let a brim ear appear.
If set to 0, no brim will be created.
If set to ~180, brim will be created on everything but straight sections.

process.label: Brim ear detection radius
process.tooltip:
The geometry will be decimated before detecting sharp angles. This parameter indicates the minimum length of the deviation for the decimation.
0 to deactivate.

process.label: Brim ears outer only
process.tooltip: Generate mouse ears only on the outer contour of the model, excluding holes and enclosed sections.

process.label: Slicing Mode
process.tooltip: Use "Even-odd" for 3DLabPrint airplane models. Use "Close holes" to close all holes in the model.

process.label: Print sequence
process.tooltip: This determines the print sequence, allowing you to print layer-by-layer or object-by-object.

process.label: Intra-layer order
process.tooltip:
Order in which object instances are visited within a single layer, which controls how much travel is spent moving between them.

Default: nearest-neighbor chaining, refined with 2-opt and crossing removal. A good general choice.
As object list: instances are printed in the same order as the object list, without any path optimization. Use it when you need a predictable, manually controlled order.
Best of all (shortest path): every strategy is evaluated and the shortest one is used. The object instance order is decided once for the whole print, while the ordering of individual islands is decided per layer, so different layers may end up using different strategies. Slightly slower to slice.
Snake: serpentine row-by-row traversal, refined with 2-opt. Well suited to regular grids of many small parts.

With multiple filaments or tools in the same layer, minimizing tool changes takes priority: objects are grouped by filament first and this setting only orders the instances within each filament group, so the overall sequence may not look like the shortest path across the plate.

process.label: Spiral vase
process.tooltip: This enables spiraling, which smooths out the Z moves of the outer contour and turns a solid model into a single walled print with solid bottom layers. The final generated model has no seam.

process.label: Smooth Spiral
process.tooltip: Smooth Spiral smooths out X and Y moves as well, resulting in no visible seam at all, even in the XY directions on walls that are not vertical.

process.label: Max XY Smoothing
process.tooltip: Maximum distance to move points in XY to try to achieve a smooth spiral. If expressed as a %, it will be computed over nozzle diameter.

process.label: Spiral starting flow ratio
process.tooltip: Sets the starting flow ratio while transitioning from the last bottom layer to the spiral. Normally the spiral transition scales the flow ratio from 0% to 100% during the first loop which can in some cases lead to under extrusion at the start of the spiral.

process.label: Spiral finishing flow ratio
process.tooltip: Sets the finishing flow ratio while ending the spiral. Normally the spiral transition scales the flow ratio from 100% to 0% during the last loop which can in some cases lead to under extrusion at the end of the spiral.

process.label: Timelapse
process.tooltip: If smooth or traditional mode is selected, a timelapse video will be generated for each print. After each layer is printed, a snapshot is taken with the chamber camera. All of these snapshots are composed into a timelapse video when printing completes. If smooth mode is selected, the toolhead will move to the excess chute after each layer is printed and then take a snapshot. Since the melt filament may leak from the nozzle during the process of taking a snapshot, a prime tower is required for smooth mode to wipe the nozzle.

process.label: Enable clumping detection
process.tooltip: Enable clumping detection

process.label: Fuzzy skin
process.tooltip: This setting makes the toolhead randomly jitter while printing walls so that the surface has a rough textured look. This setting controls the fuzzy position.

process.label: Fuzzy skin generator mode
process.tooltip:
Fuzzy skin generation mode. Works only with Arachne!
Displacement: Сlassic mode when the pattern is formed by shifting the nozzle sideways from the original path.
Extrusion: The mode when the pattern formed by the amount of extruded plastic. This is the fast and straight algorithm without unnecessary nozzle shake that gives a smooth pattern. But it is more useful for forming loose walls in the entire they array.
Combined: Joint mode [Displacement] + [Extrusion]. The appearance of the walls is similar to [Displacement] Mode, but it leaves no pores between the perimeters.

Attention! The [Extrusion] and [Combined] modes works only the fuzzy_skin_thickness parameter not more than the thickness of printed loop. At the same time, the width of the extrusion for a particular layer should also not be below a certain level. It is usually equal 15-25% of a layer height. Therefore, the maximum fuzzy skin thickness with a perimeter width of 0.4 mm and a layer height of 0.2 mm will be 0.4-(0.2*0.25)=±0.35mm! If you enter a higher parameter than this, the error Flow::spacing() will displayed, and the model will not be sliced. You can choose this number until this error is repeated.

process.label: Fuzzy skin noise type
process.tooltip:
Noise type to use for fuzzy skin generation:
Classic: Classic uniform random noise.
Perlin: Perlin noise, which gives a more consistent texture.
Billow: Similar to perlin noise, but clumpier.
Ridged Multifractal: Ridged noise with sharp, jagged features. Creates marble-like textures.
Voronoi: Divides the surface into voronoi cells, and displaces each one by a random amount. Creates a patchwork texture.
Ripple: Uniform ripple pattern that ripples left and right of the original path. Repeating pattern, woven appearance.

process.label: Fuzzy skin point distance
process.tooltip: The average distance between the random points introduced on each line segment.

process.label: Fuzzy skin thickness
process.tooltip: The width of jittering: it’s recommended to keep this lower than the outer wall line width.

process.label: Fuzzy skin feature size
process.tooltip: The base size of the coherent noise features, in mm. Higher values will result in larger features.

process.label: Fuzzy Skin Noise Octaves
process.tooltip: The number of octaves of coherent noise to use. Higher values increase the detail of the noise, but also increase computation time.

process.label: Fuzzy skin noise persistence
process.tooltip: The decay rate for higher octaves of the coherent noise. Lower values will result in smoother noise.

process.label: Number of ripples per layer
process.tooltip: Controls how many full cycles of ripples will be added per layer.

process.label: Ripple offset
process.tooltip:
Shifts the ripple phase forward along the print path by the specified percentage of a wavelength each layer period.
- 0% keeps every layer identical.
- 50% shifts the pattern by half a wavelength, effectively inverting the phase.
- 100% shifts the pattern by a full wavelength, returning to the original phase.

The shift is applied once every number of layers set by Layers between ripple offset, so layers within the same group are printed identically.

process.label: Layers between ripple offset
process.tooltip:
Specifies how many consecutive layers share the same ripple phase before the offset is applied.
For example:
- 1 = Layer 1 is printed with the base ripple pattern, then layer 2 is shifted by the configured offset, then layer 3 returns to the base pattern, and so on.
- 3 = Layers 1 to 3 are printed with the base ripple pattern, then layers 4 to 6 are shifted by the configured offset, then layers 7 to 9 return to the base pattern, etc.

process.label: Apply fuzzy skin to first layer
process.tooltip: Whether to apply fuzzy skin on the first layer.

process.label: Reduce infill retraction
process.tooltip: Don't retract when the travel is entirely within an infill area. That means the oozing can't been seen. This can reduce times of retraction for complex model and save printing time, but make slicing and G-code generating slower. Note that Z-hop is also not performed in areas where retraction is skipped.

process.label: Add line number
process.tooltip: Enable this to add line number(Nx) at the beginning of each G-code line.

process.label: Verbose G-code
process.tooltip: Enable this to get a commented G-code file, with each line explained by a descriptive text. If you print from SD card, the additional weight of the file could make your firmware slow down.

process.label: High precision G-code (experimental)
process.tooltip: Write X, Y, Z, I and J with 4 decimal places instead of 3, and E with 6 instead of 5, to reduce rounding errors in the G-code. With relative E distances, the rounding error of each move is also carried over to the next one. Supports are removed after printing, so they keep the standard precision. This may help stabilize extrusion with small nozzles (e.g. 0.2 mm) and thin layers (e.g. 0.08 mm or less), where each move extrudes so little material that rounding errors matter most. The effect depends strongly on how well the rest of the settings are tuned and may be hard to notice unless the print profile is well calibrated. The G-code file becomes about 10 percent larger, which may slow down printers that parse G-code slowly.

process.label: Label objects
process.tooltip: Enable this to add comments into the G-code labeling print moves with what object they belong to, which is useful for the Octoprint CancelObject plug-in. This setting is NOT compatible with Single Extruder Multi Material setup and Wipe into Object / Wipe into Infill.

process.label: Exclude objects
process.tooltip: Enable this option to add EXCLUDE OBJECT command in G-code.

process.label: Outline tolerance
process.tooltip: Maximum deviation of the object outline written to EXCLUDE_OBJECT_DEFINE from the original outline. Larger values give fewer points, which helps firmware that stalls while parsing G-code with many objects. 0 keeps every point.

process.label: Filename format
process.tooltip: Users can decide project file names when exporting.

process.label: Change extrusion role G-code (process)
process.tooltip: This G-code is inserted when the extrusion role is changed. It runs after the machine and filament extrusion role G-code.

process.label: Post-processing Scripts
process.tooltip: If you want to process the output G-code through custom scripts, just list their absolute paths here. Separate multiple scripts with a semicolon. Scripts will be passed the absolute path to the G-code file as the first argument, and they can access the Orca Slicer config settings by reading environment variables.

process.label: Slicing Pipeline Plugin
process.tooltip: Python plugins invoked at each slicing pipeline step to read and modify intermediate slicing data, including a final G-code post-processing step. Research/experimental.

process.label: Configuration notes
process.tooltip: You can put here your personal notes. This text will be added to the G-code header comments.

process.label: Print extruder id
process.tooltip: Print extruder id.

process.label: Print's extruder variant
process.tooltip: Print's extruder variant.

process.label: Loop pattern interface
process.tooltip: This covers the top contact layer of the supports with loops. It is disabled by default.

process.label: Belt purge tower object
process.tooltip: Marks the auto-generated belt purge prism. Managed automatically; do not set manually.

process.label: Condition
process.tooltip: A Boolean expression using the configuration values of an active printer profile. If this expression evaluates to true, this profile is considered compatible with the active printer profile.

process.label: Inherits profile
process.tooltip: Name of parent profile.

process.label: Plugins Used
process.tooltip: Plugin capabilities referenced by this preset, stored as name;uuid;capability.

process.label: Purging volumes - load/unload volumes
process.tooltip: This vector saves required volumes to change from/to each tool used on the wipe tower. These values are used to simplify creation of the full purging volumes below.

process.label: IDEX/IQEX Print Mode
process.tooltip: Name of the active IDEX/IQEX parallel print mode, or "primary" for single-carriage printing. Requires IDEX/IQEX Printer enabled in the Printer preset (Printer → Multimaterial → IDEX/IQEX Configuration).

process.label: IDEX/IQEX head filament map
process.tooltip: Per-plate override mapping physical heads to filament slots (1-based). Empty means each head uses the first filament that the printer's physical extruder map routes to it.

process.label: Ironing expansion
process.tooltip: Expand or contract the ironing area.

filament.label: Type
filament.tooltip: Filament material type

filament.label: Vendor
filament.tooltip: Vendor of filament. For show only.

filament.label: Soluble material
filament.tooltip: Soluble material is commonly used to print supports and support interfaces.

filament.label: Support material
filament.tooltip: Support material is commonly used to print supports and support interfaces.

filament.label: Filament ramming length
filament.tooltip: When changing the extruder, it is recommended to extrude a certain length of filament from the original extruder. This helps minimize nozzle oozing.

filament.label: Required nozzle HRC
filament.tooltip: Minimum HRC of nozzle required to print the filament. A value of 0 means no checking of the nozzle's HRC.

filament.label: Default color
filament.tooltip:
Default filament color.
Right click to reset value to system default.

filament.label: Diameter
filament.tooltip: Filament diameter is used to calculate extrusion variables in G-code, so it is important that this is accurate and precise.

filament.label: Adhesiveness Category
filament.tooltip: Filament category.

filament.label: Density
filament.tooltip: Filament density, for statistical purposes only.

filament.label: Shrinkage (XY)
filament.tooltip:
Enter the shrinkage percentage that the filament will get after cooling (94% if you measure 94mm instead of 100mm). The part will be scaled in XY to compensate. For multi-material prints, ensure filament shrinkage matches across all used filaments.
Be sure to allow enough space between objects, as this compensation is done after the checks.

filament.label: Shrinkage (Z)
filament.tooltip: Enter the shrinkage percentage that the filament will get after cooling (94% if you measure 94mm instead of 100mm). The part will be scaled in Z to compensate.

filament.label: Price
filament.tooltip: Filament price, for statistical purposes only.

filament.label: Softening temperature
filament.tooltip: The material softens at this temperature, so when the bed temperature is equal to or greater than this, it's highly recommended to open the front door and/or remove the upper glass to avoid clogs.

filament.label: Idle temperature
filament.tooltip: Nozzle temperature when the tool is currently not used in multi-tool setups. This is only used when 'Ooze prevention' is active in Print Settings. Set to 0 to disable.

filament.label: Pellet flow coefficient
filament.tooltip:
Pellet flow coefficient is empirically derived and allows for volume calculation for pellet printers.

Internally it is converted to filament_diameter. All other volume calculations remain the same.

filament_diameter = sqrt( (4 * pellet_flow_coefficient) / PI )

filament.label: Flow ratio
filament.tooltip: The material may have volumetric change after switching between molten and crystalline states. This setting changes all extrusion flow of this filament in G-code proportionally. The recommended value range is between 0.95 and 1.05. You may be able to tune this value to get a nice flat surface if there is slight overflow or underflow.

filament.label: Enable pressure advance
filament.tooltip: Enable pressure advance, auto calibration result will be overwritten once enabled.

filament.label: Pressure advance
filament.tooltip: Pressure advance (Klipper) AKA Linear advance factor (Marlin).

filament.label: Enable adaptive pressure advance (beta)
filament.tooltip:
With increasing print speeds (and hence increasing volumetric flow through the nozzle) and increasing accelerations, it has been observed that the effective PA value typically decreases. This means that a single PA value is not always 100% optimal for all features and a compromise value is usually used that does not cause too much bulging on features with lower flow speed and accelerations while also not causing gaps on faster features.

This feature aims to address this limitation by modeling the response of your printer's extrusion system depending on the volumetric flow speed and acceleration it is printing at. Internally, it generates a fitted model that can extrapolate the needed pressure advance for any given volumetric flow speed and acceleration, which is then emitted to the printer depending on the current print conditions.

When enabled, the pressure advance value above is overridden. However, a reasonable default value above is strongly recommended to act as a fallback and for when tool changing.

filament.label: Enable adaptive pressure advance within features (beta)
filament.tooltip:
Enable adaptive PA whenever there are flow changes in a feature, such as line width changes in a corner or overhangs.

Not compatible with Prusa printers as they pause to process PA changes, which causes delays and defects.

This is an experimental option, as if the PA profile is not set accurately, it will cause uniformity issues.

filament.label: Static pressure advance for bridges
filament.tooltip:
Static pressure advance value for bridges. Set to 0 to apply the same pressure advance as 
equivalent walls (using adaptive settings if enabled).

A lower PA value when printing bridges helps reduce the appearance of slight under-extrusion immediately after bridges. This is caused by the pressure drop in the nozzle when printing in the air and a lower PA helps counteract this.

filament.label: Adaptive pressure advance measurements (beta)
filament.tooltip:
Add sets of pressure advance (PA) values, the volumetric flow speeds and accelerations they were measured at, separated by a comma. One set of values per line. For example
0.04,3.96,3000
0.033,3.96,10000
0.029,7.91,3000
0.026,7.91,10000

How to calibrate:
1. Run the pressure advance test for at least 3 speeds per acceleration value. It is recommended that the test is run for at least the speed of the external perimeters, the speed of the internal perimeters and the fastest feature print speed in your profile (usually its the sparse or solid infill). Then run them for the same speeds for the slowest and fastest print accelerations, and no faster than the recommended maximum acceleration as given by the Klipper input shaper
2. Take note of the optimal PA value for each volumetric flow speed and acceleration. You can find the flow number by selecting flow from the color scheme drop down and move the horizontal slider over the PA pattern lines. The number should be visible at the bottom of the page. The ideal PA value should be decreasing the higher the volumetric flow is. If it is not, confirm that your extruder is functioning correctly. The slower and with less acceleration you print, the larger the range of acceptable PA values. If no difference is visible, use the PA value from the faster test
3. Enter the triplets of PA values, Flow and Accelerations in the text box here and save your filament profile.

filament.label: Activate temperature control
filament.tooltip:
Enable this option for automated chamber temperature control. This option activates the emitting of an M191 command before the "machine_start_gcode"
 which sets the chamber temperature and waits until it is reached. In addition, it emits an M141 command at the end of the print to turn off the chamber heater, if present.

This option relies on the firmware supporting the M191 and M141 commands either via macros or natively and is usually used when an active chamber heater is installed.

filament.label: Chamber temperature
filament.tooltip:
For high-temperature materials like ABS, ASA, PC, and PA, a higher chamber temperature can help suppress or reduce warping and potentially lead to higher interlayer bonding strength. However, at the same time, a higher chamber temperature will reduce the efficiency of air filtration for ABS and ASA.

For PLA, PETG, TPU, PVA, and other low-temperature materials, this option should be disabled (set to 0) as the chamber temperature should be low to avoid extruder clogging caused by material softening at the heat break.

If enabled, this parameter also sets a G-code variable named chamber_temperature, which can be used to pass the desired chamber temperature to your print start macro, or a heat soak macro like this: PRINT_START (other variables) CHAMBER_TEMP=[chamber_temperature]. This may be useful if your printer does not support M141/M191 commands, or if you desire to handle heat soaking in the print start macro if no active chamber heater is installed.

filament.label: Minimal
filament.tooltip:
This is the chamber temperature at which printing should start, while the chamber continues heating toward the "Target" chamber temperature. For example, set the Target to 60 and the Minimal to 50 to begin printing once the chamber reaches 50℃, without waiting for the full 60℃.

It sets a G-code variable named chamber_minimal_temperature, which can be passed to your print start macro or a heat soak macro, like this: PRINT_START (other variables) CHAMBER_MIN_TEMP=[chamber_minimal_temperature].

Unlike the "Target" chamber temperature, this option does not emit any M141/M191 commands; it only exposes the value to your custom G-code. It should not exceed the "Target" chamber temperature.

filament.label: Adaptive volumetric speed
filament.tooltip:
When enabled, the extrusion flow is limited by the smaller of the fitted value (calculated from line width and layer height) and the user-defined maximum flow. When disabled, only the user-defined maximum flow is applied.

Note: Experimental and incomplete feature imported from BBS. Functional for some profiles that already have the variable saved.

filament.label: Max volumetric speed
filament.tooltip: This setting is the volume of filament that can be melted and extruded per second. Printing speed is limited by max volumetric speed, in case of too high and unreasonable speed setting. This value cannot be zero.

filament.label: No cooling for the first
filament.tooltip: Turn off all cooling fans for the first few layers. This can be used to improve build plate adhesion.

filament.label: First layer fan speed
filament.tooltip:
Sets an exact fan speed for the first layer, overriding all other cooling settings. Useful for protecting 3D-printed toolhead parts (e.g. Voron-style ABS/ASA ducts) from a hot bed. A small amount of airflow cools the ducts down, without using full cooling that may in certain conditions hurt first-layer adhesion.
From the second layer onwards, normal cooling resumes.
If "Full fan speed at layer" is also set, the fan ramps smoothly from this value on the first layer up to your target by the chosen layer.
Only available when "No cooling for the first" is 0.
Set to -1 to disable it.

filament.label: Full fan speed at layer
filament.tooltip: Fan speed will be ramped up linearly from zero at layer "close_fan_the_first_x_layers" to maximum at layer "full_fan_speed_layer". "full_fan_speed_layer" will be ignored if lower than "close_fan_the_first_x_layers", in which case the fan will be running at maximum allowed speed at layer "close_fan_the_first_x_layers" + 1.

filament.label: Fan speed
filament.tooltip: Minimum speed for part cooling fan.

filament.label: Layer time
filament.tooltip: The part cooling fan will be enabled for layers where the estimated time is shorter than this value. Fan speed is interpolated between the minimum and maximum fan speeds according to layer printing time.

filament.label: Fan speed
filament.tooltip: The part cooling fan speed may be increased when auto cooling is enabled. This is the maximum speed for the part cooling fan.

filament.label: Layer time
filament.tooltip: The printing speed in exported G-code will be slowed down when the estimated layer time is shorter than this value in order to get better cooling for these layers.

filament.label: Keep fan always on
filament.tooltip: Enabling this setting means that part cooling fan will never stop entirely and will instead run at least at minimum speed to reduce the frequency of starting and stopping.

filament.label: Slow printing down for better layer cooling
filament.tooltip: Enable this option to slow printing speed down to ensure that the final layer time is not shorter than the layer time threshold in "Max fan speed threshold", so that the layer can be cooled for a longer time. This can improve the quality for small details.

filament.label: Don't slow down outer walls
filament.tooltip:
If enabled, this setting will ensure external perimeters are not slowed down to meet the minimum layer time. This is particularly helpful in the below scenarios:
1. To avoid changes in shine when printing glossy filaments
2. To avoid changes in external wall speed which may create slight wall artifacts that appear like Z banding
3. To avoid printing at speeds which cause VFAs (fine artifacts) on the external walls

filament.label: Min print speed
filament.tooltip: The minimum print speed to which the printer slows down to maintain the minimum layer time defined above when the slowdown for better layer cooling is enabled.

filament.label: Force cooling for overhangs and bridges
filament.tooltip: Enable this option to allow adjustment of the part cooling fan speed for specifically for overhangs, internal and external bridges. Setting the fan speed specifically for these features can improve overall print quality and reduce warping.

filament.label: Overhang cooling activation threshold
filament.tooltip: When the overhang exceeds this specified threshold, force the cooling fan to run at the 'Overhang Fan Speed' set below. This threshold is expressed as a percentage, indicating the portion of each line's width that is unsupported by the layer beneath it. Setting this value to 0% forces the cooling fan to run for all outer walls, regardless of the overhang degree.

filament.label: Overhangs and external bridges fan speed
filament.tooltip:
Use this part cooling fan speed when printing bridges or overhang walls with an overhang threshold that exceeds the value set in the 'Overhangs cooling threshold' parameter above. Increasing the cooling specifically for overhangs and bridges can improve the overall print quality of these features.

Please note, this fan speed is clamped on the lower end by the minimum fan speed threshold set above. It is also adjusted upwards up to the maximum fan speed threshold when the minimum layer time threshold is not met.

filament.label: Internal bridges fan speed
filament.tooltip:
The part cooling fan speed used for all internal bridges. Set to -1 to use the overhang fan speed settings instead.

Reducing the internal bridges fan speed, compared to your regular fan speed, can help reduce part warping due to excessive cooling applied over a large surface for a prolonged period of time.

filament.label: Support interface fan speed
filament.tooltip:
This part cooling fan speed is applied when printing support interfaces. Setting this parameter to a higher than regular speed reduces the layer binding strength between supports and the supported part, making them easier to separate.
Set to -1 to disable it.
This setting is overridden by disable_fan_first_layers.

filament.label: Ironing fan speed
filament.tooltip:
This part cooling fan speed is applied when ironing. Setting this parameter to a lower than regular speed reduces possible nozzle clogging due to the low volumetric flow rate, making the interface smoother.
Set to -1 to disable it.

filament.label: Fan speed
filament.tooltip:
Speed of auxiliary part cooling fan. Auxiliary fan will run at this speed during printing except the first several layers which is defined by no cooling layers.
Please enable auxiliary_fan in printer settings to use this feature. G-code command: M106 P2 S(0-255)

filament.label: Activate air filtration
filament.tooltip: Activate for better air filtration. G-code command: M106 P3 S(0-255)
Enable this to override the fan speed set in custom G-code during print.

filament.label: Fan speed
filament.tooltip: Speed of exhaust fan during printing. This speed will override the speed in filament custom G-code.
Enable this to override the fan speed set in custom G-code after print completion.

filament.label: Fan speed
filament.tooltip: Speed of exhaust fan after printing completes.

filament.tooltip: G-code added when the printer starts using this filament

filament.label: Change extrusion role G-code (filament)
filament.tooltip: This G-code is inserted when the extrusion role is changed for the active filament.

filament.label: End G-code
filament.tooltip: Add end G-code when finishing the printing of this filament.

filament.label: Minimal purge on wipe tower
filament.tooltip: After a tool change, the exact position of the newly loaded filament inside the nozzle may not be known, and the filament pressure is likely not yet stable. Before purging the print head into an infill or a sacrificial object, Orca Slicer will always prime this amount of material into the wipe tower to produce successive infill or sacrificial object extrusions reliably.

filament.label: Interface layer pre-extrusion distance
filament.tooltip: Pre-extrusion distance for prime tower interface layer (where different materials meet).

filament.label: Interface layer pre-extrusion length
filament.tooltip: Pre-extrusion length for prime tower interface layer (where different materials meet).

filament.label: Tower ironing area
filament.tooltip: Ironing area for prime tower interface layer (where different materials meet).

filament.label: Interface layer purge length
filament.tooltip: Purge length for prime tower interface layer (where different materials meet).

filament.label: Interface layer print temperature
filament.tooltip: Print temperature for prime tower interface layer (where different materials meet). If set to -1, use max recommended nozzle temperature.

filament.label: Loading speed at the start
filament.tooltip: Speed used at the very beginning of loading phase.

filament.label: Unloading speed

filament.label: Delay after unloading
filament.tooltip: Time to wait after the filament is unloaded. May help to get reliable tool changes with flexible materials that may need more time to shrink to original dimensions.

filament.tooltip: Speed used for stamping.

filament.label: Stamping distance measured from the center of the cooling tube
filament.tooltip: If set to non-zero value, filament is moved toward the nozzle between the individual cooling moves ("stamping"). This option configures how long this movement should be before the filament is retracted again.

filament.label: Enable ramming for multi-tool setups
filament.tooltip: Perform ramming when using multi-tool printer (i.e. when the 'Single Extruder Multimaterial' in Printer Settings is unchecked). When checked, a small amount of filament is rapidly extruded on the wipe tower just before the tool change. This option is only used when the wipe tower is enabled.

filament.label: Multi-tool ramming volume
filament.tooltip: The volume to be rammed before the tool change.
filament.group: Tool change parameters with multi extruder MM printers

filament.label: Multi-tool ramming flow
filament.tooltip: Flow used for ramming the filament before the tool change.
filament.group: Tool change parameters with multi extruder MM printers

filament.label: Condition
filament.tooltip: A Boolean expression using the configuration values of an active printer profile. If this expression evaluates to true, this profile is considered compatible with the active printer profile.

filament.label: Condition
filament.tooltip: A Boolean expression using the configuration values of an active print profile. If this expression evaluates to true, this profile is considered compatible with the active print profile.

filament.label: Filament notes
filament.tooltip: You can put your notes regarding the filament here.

filament.label: Filament printable
filament.tooltip: The filament is printable in extruder.

filament.label: Filament-extruder compatibility
filament.tooltip: A single 32-bit int encoding the compatibility level of a filament across all extruders (up to 10). Every 3 bits represent one extruder (bits [3*i, 3*i+2] for extruder i). 0: printable, 1: error, 2: critical warning, 3: warning, 4-7: reserved.

filament.label: For the first
filament.tooltip: Set special auxiliary cooling fan for the first certain layers.

filament.label: Fan speed
filament.tooltip: Special auxiliary cooling fan speed, effective only for the first x layers.

filament.label: Full fan speed at layer
filament.tooltip:
Auxiliary fan speed will be ramped up linearly from layer "For the first" to maximum at layer "Full fan speed at layer".
"Full fan speed at layer" will be ignored if lower than "For the first", in which case the fan will run at maximum allowed speed at layer "For the first" + 1.

filament.label: Deretraction speed
filament.tooltip: Speed for reloading filament into the nozzle. Zero means same speed of retraction.

filament.label: Retract amount after wipe
filament.tooltip:
This is the length of fast retraction after wipe, relative to retraction length.
The value will be clamped by 100% minus the retract amount before the wipe value.

filament.label: Retract amount before wipe
filament.tooltip: This is the length of fast retraction before a wipe, relative to retraction length.

filament.label: On surfaces
filament.tooltip: Enforce Z-Hop behavior. This setting is impacted by the above settings (Only lift Z above/below).

filament.label: Extra length on restart
filament.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after the travel move, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament. This setting is rarely needed.

filament.label: Retract on layer change
filament.tooltip: This forces a retraction on layer changes.

filament.label: Length
filament.tooltip: Some amount of material in extruder is pulled back to avoid ooze during long travel. Set zero to disable retraction.

filament.label: Travel distance threshold
filament.tooltip: Only trigger retraction when the travel distance is longer than this threshold.

filament.label: Retraction speed
filament.tooltip: Speed for retracting filament from the nozzle.

filament.label: Retraction Length (Toolchange)
filament.tooltip: When retraction is triggered before changing tool, filament is pulled back by the specified amount (the length is measured on raw filament, before it enters the extruder).

filament.label: Extra length on restart (Toolchange)
filament.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after changing tool, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament.

filament.label: Wipe while retracting
filament.tooltip: This moves the nozzle along the last extrusion path when retracting to clean any leaked material on the nozzle. This can minimize blobs when printing a new part after traveling.

filament.label: Z-hop height
filament.tooltip: Whenever there is a retraction, the nozzle is lifted a little to create clearance between the nozzle and the print. This prevents the nozzle from hitting the print when traveling more. Using spiral lines to lift Z can prevent stringing.

filament.label: Z-hop type
filament.tooltip: Type of Z-hop.

filament.label: Inherits profile
filament.tooltip: Name of parent profile.

filament.label: Wipe distance
filament.tooltip:
Describe how long the nozzle will move along the last path when retracting.

Depending on how long the wipe operation lasts, how fast and long the extruder/filament retraction settings are, a retraction move may be needed to retract the remaining filament.

Setting a value in the retract amount before wipe setting below will perform any excess retraction before the wipe, else it will be performed after.

filament.label: Filament's extruder variant
filament.tooltip: Filament's extruder variant.

filament.label: Ironing flow
filament.tooltip: Filament-specific override for ironing flow. This allows you to customize the ironing flow for each filament type. Too high value results in overextrusion on the surface.

filament.label: Ironing line spacing
filament.tooltip: Filament-specific override for ironing line spacing. This allows you to customize the spacing between ironing lines for each filament type.

filament.label: Ironing inset
filament.tooltip: Filament-specific override for ironing inset. This allows you to customize the distance to keep from the edges when ironing for each filament type.

filament.label: Ironing speed
filament.tooltip: Filament-specific override for ironing speed. This allows you to customize the print speed of ironing lines for each filament type.

filament.label: Long retraction when cut (beta)
filament.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retracting and cutting off the filament at a longer distance during changes to minimize purge. While this reduces flush significantly, it may also raise the risk of nozzle clogs or other printing problems.

filament.label: Retraction distance when cut
filament.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retraction length before cutting off during filament change.

filament.label: Flush volumetric speed
filament.tooltip: Volumetric speed when flushing filament. 0 indicates the max volumetric speed.

filament.label: Flush temperature
filament.tooltip: Temperature when flushing filament. 0 indicates the upper bound of the recommended nozzle temperature range.

filament.label: Flush temperature
filament.tooltip: Flush temperature used in fast purge mode.

filament.label: Wipe tower cooling
filament.tooltip: Temperature drop before entering the wipe tower.

filament.label: Extruder change
filament.tooltip: The maximum volumetric speed for ramming before extruder change, where -1 means using the maximum volumetric speed.

filament.label: Hotend change
filament.tooltip: The maximum volumetric speed for ramming before a hotend change, where -1 means using the maximum volumetric speed.

filament.label: Extruder change
filament.tooltip: To prevent oozing, the nozzle will perform a reverse travel movement for a certain period after the ramming is complete. The setting define the travel time.

filament.label: Hotend change
filament.tooltip: To prevent oozing, the nozzle will perform a reverse travel movement for a certain period after the ramming is complete. The setting define the travel time.

filament.label: Extruder change
filament.tooltip: To prevent oozing, the nozzle temperature will be cooled during ramming. Therefore, the ramming time must be greater than the cooldown time. 0 means disabled.

filament.label: Hotend change
filament.tooltip: To prevent oozing, the nozzle temperature will be cooled during ramming. Note: only a cooldown command and fan activation are triggered, reaching the target temperature is not guaranteed. 0 means disabled.

filament.label: Preheat temperature delta
filament.tooltip: Temperature delta applied during pre-heating before tool change.

filament.label: length when change hotend
filament.tooltip: When this retraction value is modified, it will be used as the amount of filament retracted inside the hotend before changing hotends.

filament.label: Hotend change
filament.tooltip: When changing the hotend, it is recommended to extrude a certain length of filament from the original nozzle. This helps minimize nozzle oozing.

filament.label: Filament change
filament.tooltip: The volume of material required to prime the extruder on the tower, excluding a hotend change.

filament.label: Hotend change
filament.tooltip: The volume of material required to prime the extruder for a hotend change on the tower.

printer.label: Parallel printheads count
printer.tooltip: Set the number of parallel printheads for machines like OrangeStorm Giga printer.

printer.label: Excluded bed area
printer.tooltip: Unprintable area in XY plane. For example, X1 Series printers use the front left corner to cut filament during filament change. The area is expressed as a polygon in the format "XxY, XxY, ...". It constrains material and model placement, but allows machine travel. Configure toolhead collision volumes separately for G-code checking and travel avoidance.

printer.label: Toolhead collision volumes
printer.tooltip: Collision volumes used for model and generated-material exclusion, G-code checking, and travel avoidance. Use "XxY, XxY, ..." for a full-height polygon or "ZMIN..ZMAX;XxY, XxY, ..." for a Z-limited volume. Separate multiple volumes with "|". These volumes are additional to the excluded bed area. Automatic arrangement conservatively uses the bounding box of a non-convex volume.

printer.label: Collision volume behavior
printer.tooltip: Choose whether all nozzles use the same collision volumes, derive toolhead-relative volumes from each nozzle's XY offset, or configure independent volumes for every extruder. In individual mode, select each extruder on the Extruder page to configure its volumes.

printer.label: Printable height
printer.tooltip: This is the maximum printable height which is limited by the height of the build area.

printer.label: Support multi bed types
printer.tooltip: Enable this option if you want to use multiple bed types.

printer.label: Best object position
printer.tooltip: Best auto arranging position in range [0,1] w.r.t. bed shape.

printer.label: Z offset
printer.tooltip: This value will be added (or subtracted) from all the Z coordinates in the output G-code. It is used to compensate for bad Z endstop position: for example, if your endstop zero actually leaves the nozzle 0.3mm far from the print bed, set this to -0.3 (or fix your endstop).

printer.label: Preferred orientation
printer.tooltip: Automatically orient STL files on the Z axis upon initial import.

printer.label: Printer structure
printer.tooltip: The physical arrangement and components of a printing device.

printer.label: G-code flavor
printer.tooltip: What kind of G-code the printer is compatible with.

printer.label: Skip G-code config block
printer.tooltip: Do not write the CONFIG_BLOCK (slicer configuration key/value pairs) into the G-code file. This can help with printers whose firmware crashes when parsing these comment lines (e.g. Anycubic go-klipper). Note: the G-code file will no longer contain slicer settings, so importing it back into OrcaSlicer will not restore the configuration.

printer.label: Pellet Modded Printer
printer.tooltip: Enable this option if your printer uses pellets instead of filaments.

printer.label: Use 3rd-party print host
printer.tooltip: Allow controlling BambuLab's printer through 3rd party print hosts.

printer.label: Printer Agent
printer.tooltip: Select the network agent implementation for printer communication.

printer.label: Use 3MF instead of G-code
printer.tooltip: Enable this if the printer accepts a 3MF file as the print job. When enabled, Orca Slicer sends the sliced file as a .gcode.3mf, instead of a plain .gcode file.

printer.label: Scan first layer
printer.tooltip: Enable this to allow the camera on the printer to check the quality of the first layer.

printer.label: Power Loss Recovery
printer.tooltip: Choose how to control power loss recovery. When set to Printer configuration, the slicer will not emit power loss recovery G-code and will leave the printer's configuration unchanged. Applicable to Bambu Lab or Marlin 2 firmware based printers.

printer.label: Disable set remaining print time
printer.tooltip: Disable generating of the M73: Set remaining print time in the final G-code.

printer.label: Enable belt printing
printer.tooltip: Enable belt printer mode. Belt printers use a conveyor belt as the build surface, tilted at an angle (typically 45 degrees). The slicer will rotate the slicing plane and transform G-code coordinates for the tilted build surface.

printer.label: Infinite Y axis
printer.tooltip: Enable infinite Y axis for belt printers. When enabled, the Y axis build volume limit is effectively removed, allowing objects of any length to be printed along the belt direction.

printer.label: Belt tilt angle
printer.tooltip: Tilt angle of the belt surface, in degrees. Most belt printers use 45°. Positive values rotate counter-clockwise looking down the positive tilt axis; the magnitude is also the physical belt tilt used for bed rendering and support gravity.

printer.label: Belt tilt axis
printer.tooltip: Axis the mesh is rotated about before slicing. This is the belt printer's tilt: an isometric (no distortion) rotation that also drives bed rendering and support gravity tilt, and that the G-code back-transform inverts before the machine-frame shear/scale and remap. X is the typical gantry tilt (belt travels along Y).

printer.label: Support Floor Z offset
printer.tooltip: Shifts the computed belt floor up or down (mm). Negative values lower the floor, allowing more supports to survive. Use this to diagnose belt floor formula issues.

printer.label: Decouple machine-frame tilt
printer.tooltip: Expert override: set the machine-frame (G-code shear/scale) tilt angle independently of the pre-slice rotation angle. When disabled, the machine-frame transform is derived from the belt tilt angle, so a single angle drives both stages. Enable only to compensate for a machine whose physical gantry tilt differs from the slicing rotation.

printer.label: Machine-frame tilt angle
printer.tooltip: Tilt angle (degrees) used to derive the machine-frame shear (cot) and scale (1/|sin|) applied to G-code. Only used when 'Decouple machine-frame tilt' is enabled; otherwise the belt tilt angle is used.

printer.label: G-code thumbnails
printer.tooltip: Picture sizes to be stored into a .gcode and .sl1 / .sl1s files, in the following format: "XxY, XxY, ..."

printer.label: Use relative E distances
printer.tooltip: Relative extrusion is recommended when using "label_objects" option. Some extruders work better with this option unchecked (absolute extrusion mode). Wipe tower is only compatible with relative mode. It is recommended on most printers. Default is checked.

printer.label: Use firmware retraction
printer.tooltip: This experimental setting uses G10 and G11 commands to have the firmware handle the retraction. This is only supported in recent Marlin.

printer.label: Time cost
printer.tooltip: The printer cost per hour.

printer.label: Build plate tilt X
printer.tooltip: Tilt angle of the build plate along the X axis. A positive value tilts the plate so the +X side is higher, shifting gravity toward -X and increasing overhangs on the +X side. A negative value tilts the -X side higher. Set to 0 for no X-axis tilt. In belt printer mode, this is automatically synced to the belt angle.

printer.label: Build plate tilt Y
printer.tooltip: Tilt angle of the build plate along the Y axis. A positive value tilts the plate so the +Y side is higher, shifting gravity toward -Y and increasing overhangs on the +Y side. A negative value tilts the -Y side higher. Set to 0 for no Y-axis tilt.

Start the fan this number of seconds earlier than its target start time (you can use fractional seconds). It assumes infinite acceleration for this time estimation, and will only take into account G1 and G0 moves (arc fitting is unsupported).
It won't move fan commands from custom G-code (they act as a sort of 'barrier').
It won't move fan commands into the start G-code if the 'only custom start G-code' is activated.
Use 0 to deactivate.

printer.label: Only overhangs
printer.tooltip: Will only take into account the delay for the cooling of overhangs.

printer.label: Fan kick-start time
printer.tooltip:
Emit a max fan speed command for this amount of seconds before reducing to target speed to kick-start the cooling fan.
This is useful for fans where a low PWM/power may be insufficient to get the fan started spinning from a stop, or to get the fan up to speed faster.
Set to 0 to deactivate.

printer.label: Minimum non-zero part cooling fan speed
printer.tooltip:
Some part-cooling fans cannot start spinning when commanded below a certain PWM duty cycle. When set above 0, any non-zero part-cooling fan command will be raised to at least this percentage so the fan reliably starts. A fan command of 0 (fan off) is always honoured exactly. This clamp is applied after every other fan calculation (first-layer ramp, layer-time interpolation, overhang/bridge/support-interface/ironing overrides), so scaling still operates within the range [this value, 100%].
If your firmware already disables the fan below a threshold (for example Klipper's [fan] off_below: 0.10 shuts the fan off whenever the commanded duty cycle is below 10%), this option and the firmware threshold should ideally be set to the same value. Matching them (e.g. off_below: 0.10 in Klipper and 10% here) guarantees the slicer never emits a non-zero value that the firmware would silently drop, and the fan never receives a value below the one you know it can actually spool at.
Set to 0 to deactivate.

printer.label: Radius
printer.tooltip: Clearance radius around extruder: used for collision avoidance in by-object printing.

printer.label: Distance to rod
printer.tooltip: Horizontal distance of the nozzle tip to the rod's farther edge. Used for collision avoidance in by-object printing.

printer.label: Height to rod
printer.tooltip: Distance from the nozzle tip to the lower rod. Used for collision avoidance in by-object printing.

printer.label: Height to lid
printer.tooltip: Distance from the nozzle tip to the lid. Used for collision avoidance in by-object printing.

printer.label: Bed mesh min
printer.tooltip: This option sets the min point for the allowed bed mesh area. Due to the probe's XY offset, most printers are unable to probe the entire bed. To ensure the probe point does not go outside the bed area, the minimum and maximum points of the bed mesh should be set appropriately. OrcaSlicer ensures that adaptive_bed_mesh_min/adaptive_bed_mesh_max values do not exceed these min/max points. This information can usually be obtained from your printer manufacturer. The default setting is (-99999, -99999), which means there are no limits, thus allowing probing across the entire bed.

printer.label: Bed mesh max
printer.tooltip: This option sets the max point for the allowed bed mesh area. Due to the probe's XY offset, most printers are unable to probe the entire bed. To ensure the probe point does not go outside the bed area, the minimum and maximum points of the bed mesh should be set appropriately. OrcaSlicer ensures that adaptive_bed_mesh_min/adaptive_bed_mesh_max values do not exceed these min/max points. This information can usually be obtained from your printer manufacturer. The default setting is (99999, 99999), which means there are no limits, thus allowing probing across the entire bed.

printer.label: Probe point distance
printer.tooltip: This option sets the preferred distance between probe points (grid size) for the X and Y directions, with the default being 50mm for both X and Y.

printer.label: Mesh margin
printer.tooltip: This option determines the additional distance by which the adaptive bed mesh area should be expanded in the XY directions.

printer.label: Nozzle HRC
printer.tooltip: The nozzle's hardness. Zero means no checking for nozzle hardness during slicing.

printer.label: Auxiliary part cooling fan
printer.tooltip: Enable this option if machine has auxiliary part cooling fan. G-code command: M106 P2 S(0-255).

printer.label: Fan direction
printer.tooltip: Cooling fan direction of the printer

printer.label: Support controlling chamber temperature
printer.tooltip:
This option is enabled if the machine supports controlling the chamber temperature
G-code command: M141 S(0-255)

printer.label: Support air filtration
printer.tooltip:
Enable this if the printer supports air filtration
G-code command: M106 P3 S(0-255)

printer.label: Use cooling filter
printer.tooltip: Enable this if the printer supports a cooling filter

printer.label: File header G-code
printer.tooltip: G-code written at the very top of the output file, before any other content. Useful for adding metadata that printer firmware reads from the first lines of the file (e.g. estimated print time, filament usage). Supports placeholders like {print_time_total_sec}, {print_time_day}, {print_time_hour}, {print_time_minute}, {print_time_sec} and {used_filament_length}.

printer.label: Start G-code
printer.tooltip: G-code added when starting a print.

default.value:
G28 ; home all axes
G1 Z5 F5000 ; lift nozzle

printer.label: End G-code
printer.tooltip: Add end G-code when finishing the entire print.

default.value:
M104 S0 ; turn off temperature
G28 X0  ; home X axis
M84     ; disable motors

printer.label: Between Object G-code
printer.tooltip: Insert G-code between objects. This parameter will only come into effect when you print your models object by object.

printer.label: Before layer change G-code
printer.tooltip: This G-code is inserted at every layer change before the Z lift.

printer.label: Layer change G-code
printer.tooltip: This G-code is inserted at every layer change after the Z lift.

printer.label: Change filament G-code
printer.tooltip: This G-code is inserted when filament is changed, including T commands to trigger tool change.

printer.label: Change extrusion role G-code
printer.tooltip: This G-code is inserted when the extrusion role is changed.

printer.label: Pause G-code
printer.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a code for the pause print. Users can insert pause G-code in the G-code viewer.

printer.label: Custom G-code
printer.tooltip: This G-code will be used as a custom code.

printer.label: Printer notes
printer.tooltip: You can put your notes regarding the printer here.

printer.label: Single Extruder Multi Material
printer.tooltip: Use single nozzle to print multi filament.

printer.label: Manual Filament Change
printer.tooltip: Enable this option to omit the custom Change filament G-code only at the beginning of the print. The tool change command (e.g., T0) will be skipped throughout the entire print. This is useful for manual multi-material printing, where we use M600/PAUSE to trigger the manual filament change action.

printer.label: Bed temperature type
printer.tooltip: This option determines how the bed temperature is set during slicing: based on the temperature of the first filament or the highest temperature of the printed filaments.

printer.label: Wipe tower type
printer.tooltip: Choose the wipe tower implementation for multi-material prints. Type 1 is recommended for Bambu and Qidi printers with a filament cutter. Type 2 offers better compatibility with multi-tool and MMU printers and provide overall better compatibility.

printer.label: Purge in prime tower
printer.tooltip: Purge remaining filament into prime tower.

printer.label: Enable filament ramming
printer.tooltip: Enable filament ramming

printer.label: Tool change on wipe tower
printer.tooltip: Force the toolhead to travel to the wipe tower before issuing the tool change command (Tx). Only relevant for multi-extruder (multi-toolhead) printers using a Type 2 wipe tower. By default Orca skips the travel on multi-toolhead machines because the firmware handles the head swap, which can result in the Tx command being issued above the printed part. Enable this option if you want the tool change to always be issued above the wipe tower instead.

printer.label: Wait for temperature on wipe tower
printer.tooltip: Pick up the new tool without waiting for it to reach printing temperature, travel to the wipe tower, and wait for the temperature there, right before purging. Ooze from the heat-up lands on the tower instead of the model, and the travel overlaps with the heating. Only relevant for multi-extruder (multi-toolhead) printers using a Type 2 wipe tower. The firmware or tool change macro must not wait for the temperature itself. When disabled, the temperature wait is issued right after the tool change command.

printer.label: Enable belt purge tower
printer.tooltip: Belt-printer replacement for the wipe/prime tower. When enabled on a belt printer, a purge prism is automatically generated next to the printed parts and filament-change purging is routed into it (the classic wipe tower cannot be used on belt printers because its G-code bypasses the belt transform). Only available on belt printers.

printer.label: Cooling tube position
printer.tooltip: Distance of the center-point of the cooling tube from the extruder tip.

printer.label: Cooling tube length
printer.tooltip: Length of the cooling tube to limit space for cooling moves inside it.

printer.label: Filament parking position
printer.tooltip: Distance of the extruder tip from the position where the filament is parked when unloaded. This should match the value in printer firmware.

printer.label: Extra loading distance
printer.tooltip: When set to zero, the distance the filament is moved from parking position during load is exactly the same as it was moved back during unload. When positive, it is loaded further, if negative, the loading move is shorter than unloading.

printer.label: High extruder current on filament swap
printer.tooltip: It may be beneficial to increase the extruder motor current during the filament exchange sequence to allow for rapid ramming feed rates and to overcome resistance when loading a filament with an ugly shaped tip.

printer.label: Filament load time
printer.tooltip: Time to load new filament when switch filament. It's usually applicable for single-extruder multi-material machines. For tool changers or multi-tool machines, it's typically 0. For statistics only.

printer.label: Filament unload time
printer.tooltip: Time to unload old filament when switch filament. It's usually applicable for single-extruder multi-material machines. For tool changers or multi-tool machines, it's typically 0. For statistics only.

printer.label: Tool change time
printer.tooltip: Time taken to switch tools. It's usually applicable for tool changers or multi-tool machines. For single-extruder multi-material machines, it's typically 0. For statistics only.

printer.label: IDEX/IQEX Printer
printer.tooltip: Enable parallel printing for printers with multiple independent carriages (IDEX, IQEX, and similar).

printer.label: Firmware-managed zones
printer.tooltip: When enabled, the slicer emits G-code with the primary zone's contents centered on bed origin (0,0). The printer firmware is responsible for placing copies/mirrors at each physical zone position. Enable only on printers whose firmware applies its own zone offsets in copy/mirror mode (e.g. RepRapFirmware IDEX duplication mode). Has no effect in Primary mode.

printer.label: Gantry Count
printer.tooltip: Number of independent Y-axis gantries. 1 for IDEX/single-rail IQEX. 2 for dual-gantry systems (divides bed into rows).

printer.label: Tools per Gantry
printer.tooltip: Number of independent toolheads per gantry along X. 2 for IDEX-style.

printer.label: Tool 0 Position
printer.tooltip: Physical position on the bed where tool T0 (index 0) is located. Determines how tool indices map to bed zones. For single-gantry setups (IDEX) only left/right matters; for dual-gantry setups (IQEX) all four corners are selectable (front = lower Y / near the operator, rear = higher Y / back of machine).

printer.label: Nozzle Clearance X
printer.tooltip: Distance (mm) from the nozzle to the collision-side carriage edge in X. Used to calculate the width of the collision exclusion strip at each X boundary.

printer.label: Nozzle Clearance Y
printer.tooltip: Distance (mm) from the nozzle to the collision-side carriage edge in Y. Used to calculate the width of the collision exclusion strip at each Y boundary.

printer.label: Safety Margin
printer.tooltip: Non-blocking advisory clearance strip (mm) drawn inside the primary zone at each carriage boundary. Parts placed within this strip will still slice; it is a visual reminder to leave extra clearance near the zone edge.

printer.label: Visualization Theme
printer.tooltip: Color theme for IDEX/IQEX bed zone visualization. Choose a colorblind-friendly theme if needed.

printer.label: Nozzle diameter
printer.tooltip: The diameter of nozzle.

printer.label: Nozzle type
printer.tooltip: The metallic material of the nozzle: This determines the abrasive resistance of the nozzle and what kind of filament can be printed.

printer.label: Nozzle volume
printer.tooltip: Volume of nozzle between the filament cutter and the end of the nozzle

printer.label: Extruder printable height
printer.tooltip: Maximum printable height of this extruder which is limited by mechanism of printer.

printer.label: Extruder collision volumes
printer.tooltip: Collision volumes used only by this extruder in individual mode. Use the same polygon and optional Z-range format as the shared collision volumes. Leave empty for no collision volumes on this extruder. Automatic arrangement conservatively uses the bounding box of a non-convex volume.

printer.label: Min
printer.tooltip: The lowest printable layer height for the extruder. Used to limit the minimum layer height when enable adaptive layer height.

printer.label: Max
printer.tooltip: The highest printable layer height for the extruder. Used to limit the maximum layer height when enable adaptive layer height.

printer.label: Retraction Length (Toolchange)
printer.tooltip: When retraction is triggered before changing tool, filament is pulled back by the specified amount (the length is measured on raw filament, before it enters the extruder).

printer.label: Extra length on restart (Toolchange)
printer.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after changing tool, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament.

printer.label: Long retraction when cut (beta)
printer.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retracting and cutting off the filament at a longer distance during changes to minimize purge. While this reduces flush significantly, it may also raise the risk of nozzle clogs or other printing problems.

printer.label: Retraction distance when cut
printer.tooltip: Experimental feature: Retraction length before cutting off during filament change.

printer.label: Emit limits to G-code
printer.tooltip:
If enabled, the machine limits will be emitted to G-code file.
This option will be ignored if the G-code flavor is set to Klipper.

printer.label: Resonance avoidance
printer.tooltip:
By reducing the speed of the outer wall to avoid the resonance zone of the printer, ringing on the surface of the model are avoided.
Please turn this option off when testing ringing.

printer.label: Min
printer.tooltip: Minimum speed of resonance avoidance.

printer.label: Max
printer.tooltip: Maximum speed of resonance avoidance.

printer.label: Emit input shaping
printer.tooltip:
Override firmware input shaping settings.
If disabled, firmware settings are used.

printer.label: Input shaper type
printer.tooltip:
Choose the input shaper algorithm.
Default uses the firmware default settings.
Disable turns off input shaping in the firmware.

Resonant frequency for the X axis input shaper.
Zero will use the firmware frequency.
To disable input shaping, use the Disable type.
RRF: X and Y values are equal.

To disable input shaping, use the Disable type.

printer.label: Support parallel printheads
printer.tooltip: Enable printer settings for machines that can use multiple printheads in parallel.

printer.label: Parallel printheads bed exclude areas
printer.tooltip: Ordered list of bed exclude areas by parallel printhead count. Item 1 applies to one printhead, item 2 to two printheads, and so on. Leave an item empty for no excluded area.

printer.label: Printer type
printer.tooltip: Type of the printer.

printer.label: Printer extruder id
printer.tooltip: Printer extruder id.

printer.label: Printer's extruder variant
printer.tooltip: Printer's extruder variant.

printer.label: Extruder variant list
printer.tooltip: Extruder variant list.

printer.label: Default Nozzle Volume Type.
printer.tooltip: Default Nozzle volume type for extruders in this printer.

printer.label: Nozzle height
printer.tooltip: The height of nozzle tip.

printer.label: Master extruder id
printer.tooltip: Default extruder id to place filament.

printer.label: Default process profile
printer.tooltip: Default process profile when switching to this machine profile.

printer.label: Inherits profile
printer.tooltip: Name of parent profile.

printer.label: Clumping detection layers
printer.tooltip: Clumping detection layers.

printer.label: Probing exclude area of clumping
printer.tooltip: Probing exclude area of clumping.

printer.label: Z-hop type
printer.tooltip: Type of Z-hop.

printer.label: Traveling angle
printer.tooltip: Traveling angle for Slope and Spiral Z-hop type. Setting it to 90° results in Normal Lift.

printer.label: On surfaces
printer.tooltip: Enforce Z-Hop behavior. This setting is impacted by the above settings (Only lift Z above/below).

printer.label: Farthest point timelapse
printer.tooltip: When enabled, the timelapse snapshot is taken at the farthest point from camera instead of traveling to the wipe tower or excess chute. Only effective in traditional timelapse mode on non-I3 printers.

printer.label: Host Type
printer.tooltip: Orca Slicer can upload G-code files to a printer host. This field must contain the kind of the host.

printer.label: Hostname, IP or URL
printer.tooltip: Orca Slicer can upload G-code files to a printer host. This field should contain the hostname, IP address or URL of the printer host instance. Print host behind HAProxy with basic auth enabled can be accessed by putting the user name and password into the URL in the following format: https://username:password@your-octopi-address/

printer.label: API Key / Password
printer.tooltip: Orca Slicer can upload G-code files to a printer host. This field should contain the API Key or the password required for authentication.

printer.label: Serial Number
printer.tooltip: Flashforge local API requires the printer serial number.

printer.label: Device UI
printer.tooltip: Specify the URL of your device user interface if it's not same as print_host.

printer.label: HTTPS CA File
printer.tooltip: Custom CA certificate file can be specified for HTTPS OctoPrint connections, in crt/pem format. If left blank, the default OS CA certificate repository is used.

printer.label: Printer
printer.tooltip: Name of the printer.

printer.label: Ignore HTTPS certificate revocation checks
printer.tooltip: Ignore HTTPS certificate revocation checks in the case of missing or offline distribution points. One may want to enable this option for self signed certificates if connection fails.

printer.label: Format of G-code thumbnails
printer.tooltip: Format of G-code thumbnails: PNG for best quality, JPG for smallest size, QOI for low memory firmware.

printer.label: Type
printer.tooltip: This setting is only used for initial value of manual calibration of pressure advance. Bowden extruder usually has larger PA value. This setting doesn't influence normal slicing.

printer.label: Map the logical extruder to physical extruder
printer.tooltip: Map the logical extruder to physical extruder.

printer.label: Default bed type
printer.tooltip: Default bed type for the printer (supports both numeric and string format).

printer.label: IDEX/IQEX Mode Names
printer.tooltip: Display names for each user-defined IDEX/IQEX parallel print mode.

printer.label: IDEX/IQEX Mode Active Tools
printer.tooltip: Tool role assignments for each mode. Format: "idx:P,idx:C,idx:M" where P=Primary, C=Copy, M=Mirror (e.g. "0:P,1:C,2:M,3:M"). Managed by the IDEX/IQEX Modes editor in the Printer preset.

printer.label: IDEX/IQEX Mode G-codes
printer.tooltip: G-code or macro call to inject at print start for each mode.

printer.label: Hotend change time
printer.tooltip: Time to change hotend.

printer.label: Support fast purge mode
printer.tooltip: Whether this printer supports fast purge mode with optimized temperature and multiplier.

printer.label: Deretraction speed (extruder change)
printer.tooltip: Speed for reloading filament into the nozzle when switching extruder.

printer.label: Elephant foot compensation
printer.tooltip: This shrinks the first layer on the build plate to compensate for elephant foot effect.

printer.label: Default filament profile
printer.tooltip: Default filament profile when switching to this machine profile.

printer.label: Deretraction speed
printer.tooltip: Speed for reloading filament into the nozzle. Zero means same speed of retraction.

printer.label: Extruder Color
printer.tooltip: Only used as a visual help on UI.

printer.label: Retract amount after wipe
printer.tooltip:
This is the length of fast retraction after wipe, relative to retraction length.
The value will be clamped by 100% minus the retract amount before the wipe value.

printer.label: Retract amount before wipe
printer.tooltip: This is the length of fast retraction before a wipe, relative to retraction length.

printer.label: Extra length on restart
printer.tooltip: When the retraction is compensated after the travel move, the extruder will push this additional amount of filament. This setting is rarely needed.

printer.label: Retract on layer change
printer.tooltip: This forces a retraction on layer changes.

printer.label: Length
printer.tooltip: Some amount of material in extruder is pulled back to avoid ooze during long travel. Set zero to disable retraction.

printer.label: Travel distance threshold
printer.tooltip: Only trigger retraction when the travel distance is longer than this threshold.

printer.label: Retraction speed
printer.tooltip: Speed for retracting filament from the nozzle.

printer.label: Wipe while retracting
printer.tooltip: This moves the nozzle along the last extrusion path when retracting to clean any leaked material on the nozzle. This can minimize blobs when printing a new part after traveling.

printer.label: Wipe distance
printer.tooltip:
Describe how long the nozzle will move along the last path when retracting.

Depending on how long the wipe operation lasts, how fast and long the extruder/filament retraction settings are, a retraction move may be needed to retract the remaining filament.

Setting a value in the retract amount before wipe setting below will perform any excess retraction before the wipe, else it will be performed after.

printer.label: Z-hop height
printer.tooltip: Whenever there is a retraction, the nozzle is lifted a little to create clearance between the nozzle and the print. This prevents the nozzle from hitting the print when traveling more. Using spiral lines to lift Z can prevent stringing.
